sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: docker run -e KEY=value passes env vars. In Dockerfile: ENV KEY=value (baked in) or ARG KEY (build-time, passed via --build-arg). docker-compose: environment: section. The app reads with os.Getenv/LookupEnv.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The four mechanisms, from build-time to runtime:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile: ENV — baked into the image (every container from it)
ENV APP_MODE=production

# Dockerfile: ARG — build-time only (not in the final image)
ARG VERSION=dev
RUN go build -ldflags="-X main.version=${VERSION}" .
```

```bash
# Run-time: -e (per-container)
docker run -e DATABASE_URL=postgres://db:5432/app -e PORT=8080 myapp
```

```yaml
# docker-compose: the environment section
services:
  app:
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://db:5432/app
      PORT: "8080"
```

The Go side (the receiver):
```go
port := os.Getenv("PORT")           // "8080"
dbURL, ok := os.LookupEnv("DATABASE_URL") // the present/absent distinction
```

The pattern (12-factor): the container is the same everywhere (the image); the ENVIRONMENT is the config — the same binary, different env vars per environment. This is the docker env's entire value: the image is immutable; the env is the deployment.

The secrets distinction: env vars are readable via docker inspect — for secrets (DB passwords), use Docker secrets (Swarm/K8s) or a vault — env vars are fine for config, wrong for credentials.

The .env file: docker run --env-file .env reads the KEY=VALUE list — the development convenience. Production env vars come from the orchestrator (Kubernetes configMap/secret).

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[ARG: build-time] --> L[ldflags: version baked in]
    E[ENV: image default] --> C[container: baked]
    RUN[docker run -e] → O[override at runtime]
    ENV-FILE[--env-file .env] → DEV[dev convenience]
    YML[compose environment:] → LOCAL[local stack]
    O --> APP[os.Getenv / LookupEnv in Go]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The ENV vs ARG distinction, mechanically: ENV values live in the image's config (every container, every start — same value). ARG values exist only DURING the build (the build's parameter) — not in the final image. The crossover: ARG VERSION + ENV APP_VERSION=${VERSION} — the build-time parameter baked into the runtime env.

The layer interaction: ENV creates a layer — changing the env in a rebuild invalidates every layer after it. Multi-stage builds mitigate (the final stage is minimal). The composition: ENV for defaults (the image's sane baseline), -e for the deployment's overrides — the precedence: run-time -e BEATS the image's ENV (the layering is deliberate).

The Go integration pattern: main reads the config env vars ONCE at startup, validates (fail fast on a missing required var), and passes the config struct everywhere. The app never re-reads os.Getenv mid-request (a config change mid-run is a different deployment — the container philosophy).
